Listen to this article Share ProvidusUnity Bank is targeting financing and trade facilitation barriers limiting Nigerian exporters’ competitiveness as it intensifies efforts to support the growth of the country’s non-oil export sector and expand businesses’ access to international markets. The bank convened more than 200 exporters, industry associations and government institutions at the fifth edition of its non-oil export business forum in Kano, where stakeholders discussed trade finance, regulatory compliance, international market requirements and practical ways to improve export performance. The engagement comes as Nigeria’s non-oil export sector records significant growth. According to the Nigerian Export Promotion Council, the country generated a record $6.1 billion in non-oil export receipts in 2025, representing an 11.5 percent increase over 2024. Export volumes also rose to 8.02 million metric tonnes, with 281 non-oil products reaching 120 countries. Despite the growth, opportunities remain to deepen local processing, improve access to trade finance, strengthen compliance with international standards and expand market access, areas considered important to sustaining export growth and improving the competitiveness of Nigerian businesses. Delivering remarks on behalf of Walter Akpani, managing director and chief executive officer of ProvidusUnity Bank, Enyinnaya Akagha, the bank’s treasurer, reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the sector through stronger stakeholder collaboration and innovative trade solutions. He said Nigeria’s non-oil export sector offered significant opportunities to diversify the economy, strengthen foreign exchange earnings and create sustainable business growth, but realising this potential required closer collaboration across the export value chain and financial solutions tailored to exporters’ needs. “As a Future Forward bank, ProvidusUnity Bank is committed to providing responsive, seamless and innovative trade solutions that help businesses overcome operational challenges, access new markets and scale internationally,” Akpani said. He added that working with exporters, industry associations and regulators would help the bank contribute to a more competitive and resilient export ecosystem. The forum brought together representatives of the Kano Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Nigerian Shippers’ Council, Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, Dawanau Market Association and the Association of Sesame Farmers. Other participants included agribusiness operators, manufacturers, leather and tannery businesses and commodity traders, reflecting the range of enterprises involved in northern Nigeria’s agricultural and industrial value chains. Abdullahi Maidoya Yakubu, chairman of the Board of Trustees of Dawanau International Market Limited, said the engagement was important to unlocking the region’s export potential. He noted that northern Nigeria had significant opportunities in agricultural commodities and other exportable products, adding that connecting exporters with financial institutions, regulators and industry experts could help businesses overcome barriers, access new markets and increase export volumes. Government and regulatory institutions represented at the forum included the Central Bank of Nigeria, Nigerian Customs Service and Nigerian Export-Import Bank. Discussions centred on trade finance, regulatory compliance, trade facilitation and international market requirements, with participants exploring ways to help exporters navigate operational challenges and compete more effectively in global markets. Abiodun Ariyo, Group head of Global Trade and Structured Finance at ProvidusUnity Bank, whose team organised the forum, said the initiative was designed to connect exporters with the knowledge, partnerships and support needed to compete internationally. He said building a competitive non-oil export sector required more than access to foreign markets, as businesses also needed appropriate financing, efficient trade processes, regulatory clarity and the capacity to meet global standards. By bringing exporters and key stakeholders together, Ariyo said, the forum provided an opportunity to address these needs and identify practical pathways for sustainable export growth. The engagement reinforces ProvidusUnity Bank’s focus on supporting businesses involved in international trade through trade finance solutions, stakeholder collaboration and initiatives aimed at promoting export growth and economic diversification.
